From the Head on the Inspection Report:
I am delighted to be able to provide you with the formal report following our recent inspection in May 2024.
To provide some context, Independent Schools are inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), regulated by the Department for Education (DfE). Whereas previously schools had a regulatory compliance inspection and a quality of education inspection, these have both now been combined into one inspection format.
The new inspection framework places the responsibility on the school’s leadership and management and governance to actively promote the wellbeing of pupils at the centre of ISI’s evaluation of the school.
The inspection focuses on safeguarding across all aspects of school and on the following four sections:
Section 1: Leadership and management, and governance.
Section 2: Pupils’ education, training, and recreation, to include pupils’ outcomes.
Section 3: Pupils’ physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing.
Section 4: Pupils’ social and economic wellbeing and contribution to society.
Inspectors look for what genuinely happens and not what schools tell them happens. They consider a range of connected evidence, including school records and by confirming the context of what inspectors are seeing, hearing and reading on inspection.
The biggest change is how the reports are written. There are no longer gradings, but instead refer only to something as being ‘good’. The focus is more on data and whether standards are met or not. Schools will then have action points if they have not met the Independent Schools Standards and the regulatory requirements. And all schools now have recommendations on things they could change / improve or introduce.
I am delighted with our report as it recognises so many of the great things we are doing as a school. I am thrilled we have no action points at all and only two recommendations which relate to how we use our data and which we already had on our development plan to review. We had conducted and continue to conduct extensive self-evaluation and we have extremely high standards, so I am ecstatic at having only two recommendations in areas that are known to us.
I am most grateful to the wonderful team at Holmewood, (teaching, admin and support) all of whom have contributed to these excellent outcomes. The children should also get a special mention; it was they who were inspected as much as the adults and the systems, and, as we knew they would, they shone!
It is as we have always believed; the children at Holmewood achieve a variety and plethora of excellent outcomes and they develop in such wonderful ways. Extraordinary lives truly do begin at Holmewood.

Welcome to Boarding at Holmewood House
As Houseparents at Holmewood House, it is our great pleasure to welcome you to our boarding family. Our aim is to create a true “home from home” for every boarder – a place where children feel safe, supported, and inspired to grow. Boarding is a unique journey, full of opportunities to make friends, explore, and take charge of their own adventure. We believe in the power of belonging, and we are committed to creating an environment that is warm, inclusive, and full of heart. From personalising bedrooms to leaving handprints on the wall, every child is encouraged to leave their mark and be proud of who they are.
Whether it’s in the classroom, on the sports field, at music concerts, or cheering each other on from the sidelines, we celebrate every success and support one another every step of the way. Our dedicated boarding team live on-site and work closely together to ensure each child’s happiness and wellbeing are at the centre of everything we do.
With the doors to our new boarding house now open, we are excited to continue building memories and traditions as part of Holmewood’s rich history. We warmly invite you to visit and experience the spirit of our boarding community for yourself.
We look forward to welcoming you.
Caolan and Isobel Houseparents

EYFS
The staff in the Early Years Foundation stage are passionate about our Early Years’ vision and what it stands for. We believe our vision is embedded in our everyday practise within our environment, both indoors in our airy classrooms as well as the outside learning environment and our extensive school grounds.
All of our classes throughout the Early Years, follow the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum. This Nursery curriculum covers 7 areas of development, catering for the different age bands that are developmental, allowing for individual progress, from birth to 5 years of age.
Through child-initiated play and adult directed activities, we provide the children with a variety of stimulating, exciting and engaging opportunities where they can explore and develop their learning experiences, helping them to make sense of the world which they live in.
Our daily routine offers small groups and individualised programmes which ensure that each child maximises their progression in a happy and organised environment whilst experiencing music, swimming, physical education and a foreign language under the structure and guidance of specialist teachers.
The children have directed teaching times: a focus activity – which is mostly topic or skill related, a phonics lesson and a maths lesson. All of these lessons are cross curricular linked as much as possible to make their learning “real “. The children enjoy a good balance of teacher directed time with their own child initiated time, where we encourage them to use the skills they have learnt at Nursery, independently, either inside or outside. The outside learning environment is an extension of our classrooms and we use our wonderful learning garden as well as the extensive school grounds during our weekly forest school excursions.
KEY STAGE 1
In Key Stage 1, our experienced staff enjoy a thorough handover with the Early Years team and create a seamless and highly successful transition out of the Early Years programme.
The children continue with phonics on a daily basis, drawing from both the Letters and Sounds scheme as well as aspects of Read Write Inc. The phonics is complemented by daily reading which is done three to four times a week on a one to one basis, but also as a group in class, during phonics and of course throughout the school day.
Both English and Maths are covered on a daily basis. Our English curriculum will incorporate writing, SPaG and also involves discreet handwriting lessons, helping the children to continue to make the transition from print to cursive script. We firmly believe that the love of writing stems from experience so you will often find our writers taking a walk around the school grounds collecting the materials to build their ‘Owl Babies’ nests, performing their ideas or finding some other way to immerse themselves in whatever they are about to write about.
In addition to these key areas, the children will be taught Science and Topic which incorporates History and Geography and is in turn, closely linked to what is being covered in science.

Nursery care that fits around your working week
Finding nursery care that genuinely works around a job is hard. At Holmewood House, our Nursery in Langton Green, Tunbridge Wells is open up to 50 weeks a year, Monday to Friday from 7.30am to 6.00pm, closing only for Christmas, Bank Holidays and three school INSET days. For working parents across Tunbridge Wells and the wider Kent area, that means dependable, high-quality early-years care that doesn’t stop at the end of term.
Our provision is fully flexible. You can book from as little as three sessions a week through to full-time, all-year-round care, and shape your child’s week around the days you actually need. It is the reassurance of a nursery and the continuity of a school, in one place.
Children can join the Nursery from the beginning of the term in which they turn three – so a child with a November birthday, for example, may start in September, before their third birthday. Our three school terms begin in September, January and April.
Term-time or all year round – you choose
Families can choose the pattern that suits them:
Please refer to the Nursery Fee Schedule for details, and contact admissions for any questions about billing or sessions.
Wraparound care, built in
Because our Nursery sits within the school day, wraparound care is simple and seamless. A breakfast club runs from 7.30am and after-school provision is available until 5.00pm or 6.00pm, so your child stays in one familiar, caring setting from early morning to early evening – no juggling, no extra drop-offs.
More than childcare
Choosing Holmewood House means your child isn’t simply being looked after – they are learning, playing and growing within the Early Years Foundation Stage, with specialist lessons in music, swimming, PE, Forest School and French from Nursery, all delivered by qualified teachers. It is the breadth of a prep school combined with the flexibility working families need.
Funded early education
Every family is entitled to 15 hours of funded early education per week in term time, which can be used alongside your chosen sessions. Your child is eligible from the term after their third birthday. Our admissions team can talk you through how the funding works with both term-time and 50-week options.

pageCache.text:
Year 5 & 6: A Journey of Independence and Exploration
Years 5 and 6 bring exciting changes for children joining our school or moving up from Year 4. These years mark a significant increase in pupils’ independence.
Increased Independence
From Year 5, children navigate the school independently, attending classes with specialist subject teachers in humanities, science, maths, English, French, computing & digital innovation, and DT & engineering, along with sport, music, art, and drama. Each pupil has a locker and signs in and out independently with their Form Teacher.
Boarding Opportunities
An exciting change for Year 5 is the opportunity to board as a full, weekly, or flexi boarder. More details are on our Boarding pages.
The Tutor System
Each child from Year 5 is assigned a Tutor for academic, social, and emotional support, meeting fortnightly to discuss concerns and celebrate successes.
Academic Structure
In Year 5, there are sets for Maths, and pupils prepare for the ISEB Pre-Test or 11+ exams, usually taken in Autumn of Year 6. Homework is assigned four evenings a week, including sessions for reading and revision. From Year 6, pupils use laptops in most lessons, with assignments set in Microsoft Teams. Sets expand to include English, science, and humanities.
Learning Hub
The Learning Hub becomes a daily feature, with independent access to the library catalogue for reading needs.
Exciting Trips and Activities
Trips encourage exploration of culture, nature, collaboration, and teamwork culminating in a three-day camping trip in Year 6.
Games sessions include team sports like hockey, netball, football, cricket, and rugby, with PE adding activities like basketball, fitness, and tennis.
From Year 5, children engage in a carousel of enrichment activities, covering cultural enrichment, careers, finance/business, and world-readiness. The “World of Languages and Languages of the World” program offers alternatives to French, Spanish, and Classics.

In 1827 Decimus Burton, famous for many buildings in London (including the archway at Hyde Park Corner) and in Tunbridge Wells, designed and built a house in classical style and called it Mitchells after a Tudor farmhouse that had once stood on the site. Sadly in 1837 the building was destroyed by fire, but it was rebuilt and given the name by which we know it today – Holmewood House.
The House at first belonged to Sir Charles Locock, who was gynaecologist and physician to Queen Victoria. It was sold in 1850 to the Barrow family who used it as their country home until the 1930s. In 1939 The Hill School for Girls moved for a short time to Holmewood from Westerham.
Holmewood House Boys’ Preparatory School was founded during the autumn of 1945 by John and Mary Collings and Andy Trotter, and it began with just eight pupils. When the school first opened the world was vastly different, there was still rationing and school equipment was very scarce. The seams of soccer and cricket balls were frequently re-sewn by hand with fishing line, and the staff were not paid until the end of each term. The boys enjoyed listening to ‘Dick Barton, Special Agent’ on the wireless loudspeaker system which was wired through to the dormitories.
By 1950 there were 100 boys in the school and a waiting list that stretched into 1956. By 1970, Holmewood’s 25th year, numbers were over 350, necessitating a huge building programme of new classrooms, long-awaited assembly hall and music rooms. The first five year olds joined the school in 1978 when the Pre-Prep department was started.
David Ives was appointed headmaster in 1980. Along with Rachel Ives, he oversaw many changes at the school during his eighteen year tenure including the introduction of girls to the school in 1990. After only two years, the 100th girl arrived at Holmewood, and the neighbouring Knowle Court School was purchased, soon to be re-opened as the Pre-Prep department
During the nineties, Holmewood became a fully co-educational day and boarding preparatory school. Set in 32 acres of beautiful countryside on the Kent/Sussex borders, the school boasts outstanding facilities, including a 360-seat theatre, a purpose-built music school, a magnificent sports hall, a TigerTurf all-weather pitch with athletics track, an indoor .22 calibre shooting range, squash courts and a wonderful indoor swimming pool.
In July 2010, Andrew Corbett retired after twelve years as Headmaster and James Marjoribanks took up the helm, to be succeeded in September 2017 by Scott Carnochan. Ruth O’Sullivan became the first female Head to be appointed to Holmewood in March 2022.
At the start of the Autumn term in September 2011, the first lessons took place in the Collings Building, our state-of-the-art classroom block, and in 2017 the Cloisters building, incorporating eight more classrooms, two computer rooms and a learning hub, opened.

pageCache.pageTitle: Awards & Bursaries For Year 7 Entry | Kent Prep School | Holmewood House School
pageCache.text:
Scholarships and awards at Holmewood House
At Holmewood House, we recognise and nurture pupils who show outstanding ability and potential – whether in the classroom, on the stage, in the studio or on the sports field. Our scholarship and award programme celebrates excellence across the curriculum, while our bursaries open the school up to families who might not otherwise be able to join us.
There are two distinct forms of support. Scholarships and awards recognise talent and dedication in a particular discipline. Bursaries are means-tested financial support with school fees. The two can work together: where appropriate, a scholarship pupil who needs financial help can also be considered for bursarial support.
Scholarship Readiness Award for Year 7 Entry
Our Scholarship Readiness Award recognises pupils in Years 7 and 8 who show outstanding ability across different areas of the curriculum, and prepares them to compete confidently for scholarships to their senior schools.
The Scholarship Readiness Award is available to children entering Year 7 (11+). The deadline for application is 31st January of Year 6, with assessments taking place in the Spring Term – usually in March, for entry the following September. Prospective pupils joining the school are also welcome to apply at this time via admissions.
Scholarship subjects
Children who demonstrate outstanding ability, dedication and potential are invited to pursue a scholarship in one or more of the following areas:
For full details, please read our Scholarship Readiness Brochure, which sets out what the programme involves for pupils and families.
Academic
Art
Design Technology / Engineering
Drama
Music
What a Scholarship Involves
Pupils invited onto the scholarship programme are expected to show real commitment and maturity in their approach to learning, dedicating time and effort to their discipline. Whatever their subject, scholars can expect to take part in a weekly Scholarship Club, attend enrichment opportunities including off-site trips and visiting speakers, and develop their leadership skills by championing their discipline within the school.
There is no remuneration for the Scholarship Readiness programme. Instead, scholars are given access to a range of enriching opportunities at no extra cost – the reward is the experience, the challenge and the preparation for senior-school scholarships.
Where a family needs financial support, and where appropriate, the scholarship programme can be tied to our bursarial support (see below).
Scholarships to Senior Schools
Holmewood House has a strong record of preparing pupils to win scholarships and awards to leading senior schools. Our Scholarship Readiness programme is designed to give talented children the confidence, breadth and polish they need to succeed at 11+ and 13+, whether their strength is academic, sporting, musical, dramatic or artistic.
You can see where our leavers go, and the scholarships and awards they have achieved, on our Destination Schools page.
Bursarial Awards
The Governors of Holmewood House are committed to broadening access to the school by offering means-tested financial support with school fees to eligible parents. This support is known as a Bursarial Award.
Bursaries are available from Year 3 onwards. They are means-tested, and the assessment of need is undertaken by an external company to ensure transparency and fairness. This company will, following their assessment, make a recommendation to the school for their consideration.
Bursaries are usually offered for twelve months at a time, after which families are required to provide updated information about their financial circumstances.
How to apply
If you are interested in applying for a scholarship, award or bursary, please contact our admissions team, who will take your details and guide you through the process for 2026 entry: admissions@holmewoodhouse.co.uk.
Please also review our Scholarship Readiness Awards and Bursaries policy.

pageCache.text:
Holmewood House Preparatory School is one of the UK’s leading Prep Schools, feeding to the major public schools in England and we welcome applications for places for children of families currently resident overseas requiring visa sponsorship.
We can sponsor your child for a place as a day pupil, if one parent wishes to accompany him/her to the UK.
We are also very proud of the Boarding tradition at Holmewood. We strongly believe that Boarding gives children a chance to make even greater use of the school’s extensive facilities and beautiful location. A busy and fun-filled activity programme throughout the whole week gives boarders time to enjoy each other’s company and build relationships that will stand the test of time. We have a thriving, busy environment and we need to ensure that your child can adequately access our broad curriculum and benefit from the educational opportunities on offer, from an English language and general academic point of view.
If you are resident overseas and wish to enquire about a place for your child, please contact admissions at: admissions@holmewoodhouse.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care in Boarding | Holmewood House
pageCache.text:
Pastoral care is at the heart of Holmewood House boarding. Every child is known, supported, and valued for who they are.
Individual care and attention for every boarder
Our boarding house is cosy, welcoming, and full of care. Whether a child boards full-time, weekly, or flexibly, they are seen as individuals. Houseparents, tutors and staff notice the small changes, celebrate successes, and step in with support when needed. This daily attentiveness builds a strong foundation of trust and reassurance.
A community that feels like family
Boarding at Holmewood is about belonging. Shared routines, traditions, and laughter create a steady rhythm where children feel part of something bigger. Many boarders tell us that the boarding house is where they’ve grown the most — gaining independence while knowing they’re never alone.
Wellbeing support that grows with each child
Pastoral care at Holmewood extends beyond the boarding house. Our wellbeing provision includes counselling, play therapy, therapy dogs, and structured mentoring sessions with staff. This holistic approach ensures pupils have the emotional support and practical guidance they need, whether facing an academic challenge or the ups and downs of growing up.
We warmly invite you to visit Holmewood House and experience boarding for yourself. Arrange a visit today.

pageCache.text:
Nurturing Relationships and Holistic Development at Holmewood
At Holmewood, we take immense pride in the strong, positive relationships between our staff and pupils. These bonds are built on warmth, respect, kindness, and care. Your child’s welfare is our top priority. We celebrate individuality and success in all its forms.
We provide various avenues for students to express their feelings, including weekly blob trees and bi-weekly one-on-one sessions with tutors. Regular check-ins throughout the day further strengthen the pupil-teacher connection. Our Student Councils and leadership opportunities ensure that every pupil’s voice is heard and needs are met.
Our robust pastoral care system includes 1:1 assigned Tutors and Heads of Year, offering additional support. We have approachable staff and therapy dogs available for comfort, and safety circles that encourage pupils to identify trusted individuals to talk to, highlighting the importance of open communication. Our unique “My Heart” curriculum enhances emotional well-being and social development, covering themes of health, well-being, relationships, and living in the wider world.
Holmewood provides on-site play therapy and counselling, as well as mental health awareness classes, recognizing the need for extra support at any stage.
With our comprehensive approach, including an engaging curriculum, supportive teachers, and diverse co-curricular activities, every child can thrive in a safe and happy environment. At Holmewood, children gain essential skills and values to face future challenges in both their academic and personal lives.

pageCache.text:
Drama at Holmewood House
Holmewood House School offers an exceptional drama provision, featuring a comprehensive and practical curriculum designed to immerse children in the world of theatre. With professional drama teachers who have close links to the theatre industry, the school provides a rich environment for aspiring actors and technicians. Holmewood House also supports its pupils through a drama scholarship programme, with past pupils securing roles in major productions such as “Harry Potter and the Cursed Child” in the West End.
Self-expression for all
At Holmewood House School, drama is for everyone, offering benefits for all pupils, fostering self-expression, confidence, and a range of performance skills.
Children engage in an enriching curriculum covering miming, improvisation, devising, scripted work, breaking the fourth wall, and performance. All lessons are conducted on the stage of the school’s 350-seat theatre, emphasising a hands-on approach.
Performances
Each year group from Pre Nursery to Year 8 stages a main performance, allowing children to choose roles that match their comfort level and passion. Highlights include the annual musical theatre production, which is a highly anticipated event with packed audiences. Recent productions such as “Legally Blonde” and “A Touch of Snow White” have seen enthusiastic participation from children across all year group, supported by a rich collection of costumes and impressive set designs crafted by the school’s maintenance team and art department. Additionally, a professional technician trains students interested in backstage roles, ensuring a well-rounded theatrical education.
Enhancing Learning Through Experiences
To enhance their learning, children attend theatre trips and workshops, experiencing professional performances and techniques. This hands-on approach allows pupils to learn directly from the best in the industry.
LAMDA Training
Holmewood also boasts two LAMDA teachers who provide training in acting, public speaking, verse & prose, and musical theatre, achieving a 100% pass rate in recent exams. This specialised training ensures that students not only excel in their performance skills but also in their confidence and communication abilities.
